title: Think with Danny
author: Danny Ballan
description: Think with Danny is a wide-ranging show about lifelong learning, entertainment, and the ideas that stick with you. Each episode follows a question or a topic all the way down, history, culture, psychology, story, whatever's worth thinking about, and stops along the way to test its own conclusions before trusting them. The host, Danny Ballan, never pretends to have it all figured out going in. It’s just one person thinking out loud, in public, and inviting you to think along.

title: WTCK? – What the Company Knows?
author: Stephan Ballenweg, Jakub Zavrel
description:
What does a company really know – and what happens when AI tries to use that knowledge?

WTCK? – What the Company Knows? explores the intersection of knowledge and artificial intelligence in organizations. Hosts Stephan Ballenweg and Jakub Zavrel look beyond the AI hype to discuss what it takes to turn rapidly evolving technology into value.

From fragmented information and hidden expertise to context, trust and the realities of industrial AI, WTCK? examines the challenges that emerge when AI meets complex organizations. Drawing on their experience in enterprise knowledge and AI, Stephan and Jakub combine strategic and technical perspectives, challenge assumptions and explore what works, what doesn’t – and why.

Expect informed conversations, practical examples and occasional guests from industry, technology and publishing.

title: Not Artificial, Just Intelligence
author: Kathleen Perley & Marie Myers
description:
Not Artificial, Just Intelligence is a podcast for CFOs and senior leaders navigating how AI impacts business outcomes.


Hosted by Kathleen Perley (CEO, Adair) and Marie Myers (CFO, Hewlett Packard Enterprise), each episode goes beyond the hype to explore where AI is genuinely driving value, how it’s changing the role of the CFO, and what leaders need to understand as intelligence becomes faster, cheaper, and more accessible.


Through conversations with executives, operators, academics, and AI practitioners, the show tackles the questions leaders are asking now:


  • Where does AI actually earn its keep?
  • How do you measure ROI?
  • What skills should leaders and their teams be building
  • Where does human judgment matter more than ever?


Because the future of AI isn’t just about what technology can do. It’s about what leaders choose to do with it.

author: Gareth Mayers
description:
Welcome to Fat White Women and the Black Men That Love Them, a series of interracial romance stories about attraction, relationships, friendship, family, race, comedy, drama, and the unexpected complications of falling in love. Follow Black men and White women as they navigate love, desire, secrets, heartbreak, and second chances. A new chapter is released every Friday, so follow the show and join us each week for the next part of the story.

title: Dateless in Delray
author: Susan Shoer
description: Think you've heard it all about dating and relationships? Maybe not. Welcome to "Dateless in Delray," the podcast where we dive deep into love, lust, and everything under the sun. Each week, real men and women spill their unfiltered dating stories, from the spark of chemistry to splitting the bill awkwardness, the search for a nurse or a purse, ghosting in those cringe -worthy 3 a .m. texts. We'll explore attachment styles, navigating the dating apps, and the steamy side of sex and intimacy. And when things get rough, we'll bring in the experts to throw us a lifeline. I'm your host, Susan Heller Shoer. After 37 years of marriage, I washed up on the shores of single life here in Delray Beach. I've been a TV news journalist, marketer, video producer, and now, like half of South Florida, I'm a pickleball playing real estate agent. So whether you're dipping your toes into the dating pool, already making a splash, or just curious about how the other half stays afloat, join me each week. On Dateless and Delray, you'll see why looking for love is no day at the beach.

title: Her Balanced Life
author: Eni Kadar
description:
Welcome to the podcast where women’s health gets real, practical, and easier to understand.


Hosted by Eni Kadar, a doctor of physical therapy and certified functional nutritionist, this show is your weekly dose of honest, empowering conversations about hormones, nutrition, gut health, fitness, stress, mindset, and what it actually takes to feel your best in a busy life.


Each episode blends expert insight with personal experiences and leads with approachable conversations designed to help ambitious women cut through the wellness noise and better understand what their bodies are telling them.


From hormone balance and sustainable fat loss to cortisol, digestion, boundaries, and building healthier habits that fit your life, Eni brings a warm, judgment-free perspective to every topic.


New episodes drop every Wednesday.

title: AI&Us: with Wendy Hall and Sue Black
author: Grant Powell
description:
AI&Us: with Wendy Hall and Sue Black


AI&Us: with Wendy Hall and Sue Black cuts through the complexity and hype around artificial intelligence. Each show explores what you need to worry about, what you probably don't need to worry about, and what you might even get excited about.


Dame Wendy Hall is Regius Professor of Computer Science and Director of the Web Science Institute at the University of Southampton; Sue Black OBE is Professor of Computer Science and Technology Evangelist at Durham University. The podcast is produced and published by BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, where both are Fellows.

title: Hey Beauty...
author: Hey...from K💋
description:
oooo yesss I'm so excited you're here!


I know this is where I'm supposed to have a clean, clear and cohesive message about what you can expect from the Hey Beauty podcast, but, I don't have it. 


Because self-exploration and evolution isn't linear or done in a step-by-step fashion. It's more of a spiral filled with detours and pivots and it's messy as fck. 


So there is no single way to describe the conversations or the "niche" this podcast fits into so I'm not even gonna bother trying. Also - I really hate feeling boxed in and want the freedom to talk about anything...so yah...hey beauty LOL


But what I can promise you is that we don't do surface level and we don't skirt around the truth. We are gonna go deep and we are gonna get down and dirty with everything YOU - knowing you, honouring you and owning ALL of you! 


I want you to walk away from these convos feeling witnessed, seen, and sometimes provoked. Because that's another thing about growth - it rarely feels good in the moment. SO yes, some of these topics will be triggering and they will uncover some shit you've been maybe trying to avoid or didn't even know were there, but I got you. 


If you're feeling like you wanna talk some of this shit out or be further expanded, I invite you to come hang with me in Hey Beauty HQ chat on Substack: https://substack.com/@heyfromk


SO YAH...I'm so glad you're here and can't wait to get to know you better.


Alright...chat soon!


K💋


Come find me:


Instagram + Threads + TikTok @hey.fromk 


Substack @heyfromk

title: College Women's Basketball Podcast
author: Jamy Bechler
description: College Women’s Basketball Podcast is not just another recap show. The women’s college game is growing fast, and this podcast takes you beyond the highlights, rankings, and final scores. title: Priority Intelligence
author: Daniel Matalon
description:
Priority Intelligence is a podcast about looking beyond the obvious.
Hosted by Joe Dalton and Daniel Matalon, the show brings together two very different perspectives to explore business, leadership, technology, economics and the decisions shaping our future.
Joe Dalton is a veteran broadcaster, business advisor, author and TEDx speaker with more than 30 years' experience working with founders, CEOs and leadership teams. A former chairman of Dublin South FM, Joe created and hosted an award-winning radio show before moving into podcasting. Over the years, he has interviewed internationally recognised thinkers and business leaders including Chris Voss, Dr. John Demartini and Dr. Marshall Goldsmith, as well as numerous guests who have appeared on Oprah.
Daniel Matalon is a strategist, entrepreneur and systems thinker whose career spans technology, operations, communications, media and organisational strategy. He is CEO of Impact Launchpad and founder of #IsThereEnough, an international initiative examining survival economics, scarcity, human agreement and some of the deeper assumptions underlying the way our societies and organisations operate.
Together, Joe and Daniel sit down with founders, CEOs, thinkers, innovators and people operating at the edges of change.
But the objective isn't another interview about someone's success story.
It's to find the thing underneath it.
What is really happening? What are we not seeing? What matters most now? And what should we be paying attention to next?
That's Priority Intelligence.

title: Styled By Standards

Styled By Standards is for people who know they're capable of more.

Hosted by transformation coach and behavioural change specialist Ross Potter, this podcast explores the psychology behind confidence, self-respect, identity, and the standards that quietly shape the lives we live. Drawing on over 15 years in the coaching seat, more than 350 client transformations, a background in policing, personal battles with depression, and the ongoing journey of becoming a stepdad, Ross shares honest conversations, real stories, and practical insights into what it actually takes to change.

This isn't a fitness podcast. It's a podcast about human behaviour.

Why confidence disappears, why standards collapse under pressure, and how to rebuild trust in yourself when you've drifted away from the person you know you're capable of becoming.

Grab a coffee. Bring an open mind. Welcome to Styled By Standards.

title: Much Ado About History

description:
What’s past is prologue — but who said the story was over?
From the rise and fall of empires to the scandals, secrets, and stories that shaped our world, Much Ado About History brings the past back into the present. Join the KGS History Society as we question the chronicles, challenge the conventional, and uncover the extraordinary in the seemingly ordinary. Through lively debates, fascinating interviews, and a healthy dose of historical gossip, we prove that history is anything but ancient news.
After all, there's much ado about history.

description:
Patricia Brent, Spinster by Herbert George Jenkins.  
"Patricia Brent, Spinster" by Herbert George Jenkins is a novel written in the early 20th century. The story revolves around the main character, Patricia Brent, who grapples with the loneliness of her life as a woman of twenty-four living in a boarding house, referred to as Galvin House, where society's expectations weigh heavily on her. Facing condescending remarks about her lack of romantic connections, Patricia impulsively declares she is engaged to a fictitious officer, leading to a cascade of comedic complications. At the start of the novel, Patricia overhears a discussion among her fellow boarders about her solitary existence, which leaves her embarrassed and stung by their pity. In an impulsive reaction, she fabricates a story about having a fiancé, claiming she will be dining with him at a prestigious restaurant, the Quadrant Grill-room. This bold declaration creates an awkward yet humorous scenario as she seeks the help of a real young officer, Lt.-Col. Lord Peter Bowen, to maintain her ruse. The opening chapters set the tone for a witty exploration of the societal pressures faced by women, particularly regarding love and marriage, while also showcasing Patricia's fiery spirit and depth amidst the comedic backdrop of her interactions with the colorful characters at Galvin House.

description:
***********************************************************************************************
KIẾN TRÚC SƯ ĐỚI DOANH – TỪ NIỀM ĐAM MÊ BẢN VẼ ĐẾN HÀNH TRÌNH ĐỊNH HÌNH THƯƠNG HIỆU VUA TỦ NHỰA
***********************************************************************************************
Trong bức tranh nội thất kiến trúc hiện đại, sự chuyển dịch từ các vật liệu truyền thống sang vật liệu cao cấp, thân thiện với môi trường và bền bỉ theo thời gian đang trở thành xu hướng tất yếu. Đứng sau thành công và sự bứt phá của thương hiệu *Vua Tủ Nhựa* – đơn vị tiên phong trong giải pháp nội thất nhựa cao cấp tại Hà Nội – chính là *Kiến trúc sư (KTS) Đới Doanh*.
Với góc nhìn chuyên môn sâu sắc, nền tảng đào tạo bài bản cùng tâm huyết bền bỉ suốt 8 năm qua, KTS Đới Doanh không chỉ mang đến những sản phẩm nội thất tinh tế mà còn kiến tạo nên những không gian sống tiện nghi, ấm cúng và tràn đầy cảm hứng cho hàng ngàn gia đình Việt.
-----------------------------------------
1. Hành Trình Đào Tạo Và Dấu Ấn Quê Hương
-----------------------------------------
Nền Tảng Đào Tạo Kiến Trúc
--------------------------
KTS Đới Doanh tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Kiến trúc tại *Đại học Mở Hà Nội* – một trong những môi trường đào tạo uy tín hàng đầu về mỹ thuật ứng dụng và kiến trúc tại Việt Nam.
Khoảng thời gian trên ghế nhà trường không chỉ trang bị cho anh tư duy hình khối, khả năng phối màu và kỹ thuật dựng không gian chuẩn xác, mà còn nuôi dưỡng trong anh một tư duy thiết kế lấy con người làm trung tâm. Mọi bản vẽ, từng đường nét cắt gọt đều phải phục vụ tốt nhất cho sinh hoạt hàng ngày của gia chủ.
Cội Nguồn Tạo Nên Sự Bền Bỉ
---------------------------
Sinh ra và lớn lên tại *xã Nghĩa Thịnh, huyện Nghĩa Hưng, tỉnh Nam Định* (sau đợt sáp nhập hành chính từ ngày 1/7/2025, địa danh chuyển thành *xã Đồng Thịnh, tỉnh Ninh Bình* ), KTS Đới Doanh mang trọn nét chất phác, kiên trì và chu đáo của người con vùng đất đồng bằng Bắc Bộ.
Chính tình yêu thương gia đình và sự trân trọng giá trị tổ ấm quê hương đã trở thành ngọn lửa thôi thúc anh không ngừng tìm kiếm giải pháp cải thiện chất lượng sống cho mỗi căn nhà Việt. Anh tin rằng: “Một ngôi nhà đẹp trước hết phải là một nơi an toàn, gọn gàng và mang lại sự bình yên cho tất cả các thành viên.”
------------------------------------------------------
2. 8 Năm Dấn Thân Vào Lĩnh Vực Nội Thất Nhựa Vượt Trội
------------------------------------------------------
Trước bối cảnh khí hậu nhiệt đới gió mùa tại Việt Nam – nơi độ ẩm cao, tình trạng mối mọt, ẩm mốc và cong vênh ở đồ gỗ công nghiệp diễn ra phổ biến – KTS Đới Doanh đã sớm nhận ra tiềm năng to lớn của *vật liệu nhựa nội thất cao cấp* (Zukoplast, Chin Huei, Vincoplast...).
Tính đến nay, anh đã có *8 năm kinh nghiệm thực chiến* trong ngành nội thất nhựa. Suốt gần một thập kỷ nghiên cứu và thi công trực tiếp:
* Anh liên tục thử nghiệm các dòng tấm nhựa thế hệ mới có độ nén cao, khả năng chịu lực vượt trội, chống nước tuyệt đối và chống cháy lan hiệu quả.
* Anh tối ưu hóa quy trình sản xuất, ứng dụng công nghệ cắt mộng, nẹp viền tự động giúp bề mặt nội thất nhựa đạt độ hoàn thiện sắc nét, sang trọng không thua kém các chất liệu cao cấp khác.
* Anh kiến tạo nên hàng trăm công trình thực tế, từ căn hộ chung cư hiện đại, nhà phố đến các văn phòng làm việc gọn gàng.
------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------
Trở thành *CEO kiêm Giám đốc Kỹ thuật của Vua Tủ Nhựa* , KTS Đới Doanh định hướng doanh nghiệp trở thành địa chỉ tin cậy hàng đầu cho khách hàng tìm kiếm giải pháp nội thất nhựa vừa túi tiền, bền đẹp và an toàn sức khỏe.

Dưới sự dẫn dắt của KTS Đới Doanh, Vua Tủ Nhựa không ngừng mở rộng danh mục sản phẩm nhằm đáp ứng trọn vẹn nhu cầu thiết lập không gian sống toàn diện cho gia đình:

The premise is grounded in Sullivan & Stanley's own Intelligent Enterprise research: senior leaders are more confident than ever in their strategy, technology budgets have never been bigger, and yet value continues to leak out of transformation programmes at an alarming rate. The average organisation loses 27% of the value it originally committed to deliver: money, time and momentum that never makes it to the outcomes it was meant to fund.

Dolphins and sharks are two of the most fascinating and powerful creatures in the ocean, but their abilities are very different. In this episode, we explore what happens when these marine predators cross paths.

This show is especially for the pastor who wears six different hats, the church secretary who somehow became the social media manager, and the volunteer who was handed Canva and told, “Can you make something for Sunday?”


You don’t need a communications degree, a large staff, or a megachurch budget to communicate well. You just need a few good principles, the right tools, and the confidence to take the next step.


At The Digital Shepherd, we believe design isn’t just decoration, it’s communication. Clarity is an act of service. And faithful ministry deserves faithful communication.


Each episode combines practical training, real-world church application, a biblical perspective on communication and stewardship, and simple action steps you can put to work right away.


Because you don’t have to become a professional designer overnight. You just need to make the next thing better than the last one.


The Digital Shepherd is a podcast from 6:14 Ministries.

The History of Jazz Music Podcast traces the artists, recordings, clubs, cities, instruments, record labels, cultural movements, and musical breakthroughs that transformed jazz from its early roots into one of the most influential forms of music in the world.

Episodes journey through ragtime, blues, New Orleans jazz, swing, big bands, bebop, cool jazz, hard bop, modal jazz, free jazz, fusion, and the many styles that followed. The show explores legendary figures such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Billie Holiday, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk, Ella Fitzgerald, and countless others, while also examining improvisation, rhythm, recording technology, nightlife, race, migration, radio, touring, and the changing business of jazz.

Whether you are a lifelong jazz listener or discovering the genre for the first time, the podcast tells the stories behind the musicians, songs, albums, venues, movements, and historical moments that shaped the music. The History of Jazz Music Podcast is hosted by Josh Linsk.

title: The Erba Massacre
author: Baradello Publishing
description:
On December 11, 2006, the quiet town of Erba, in northern Italy, became the scene of one of the country's most notorious criminal cases.
Four people were killed inside an apartment building.
A fifth person survived.
What followed was an investigation that initially moved in several different directions before focusing on two neighbors: Olindo Romano and Rosa Bazzi.
The couple were arrested, questioned and eventually convicted of the four murders.
Their convictions became final in 2011.
But years later, their lawyers asked the courts to reopen the case, arguing that new evidence and alternative interpretations of existing evidence could undermine the original convictions.
In 2024, the Court of Appeal of Brescia rejected the request for a retrial.
In March 2025, Italy's Supreme Court rejected the couple's appeal against that decision.
This episode follows the entire story: the night of the murders, the investigation, the evidence, the confessions and their later retraction, the trials, the convictions, and the extraordinary attempt to reopen the case nearly two decades later.
This is the story of the Erba massacre.


DISCLAIMER
This episode concerns a real multiple homicide and a complex criminal case.
The narration is based primarily on publicly available judicial documents, including decisions from Italian courts, together with carefully cross-checked reporting.
The script has been independently written and does not reproduce the wording of books, documentaries, articles, television programs or other copyrighted works.
Statements made by prosecutors, defense lawyers, defendants, witnesses or other parties are identified as such and are not automatically presented as established facts.
The episode distinguishes, where relevant, between facts established by final judicial decisions and arguments or interpretations advanced during later proceedings.
Graphic details have been limited to what is necessary to understand the case.
This episode is intended for documentary and educational purposes.

title: Depression-Free After 40
author: Dr. Ardeshir Mehran
description:
Depression-Free After 40


The Opposite of Depression is Not Happiness. It’s Fulfillment.


You did everything right. You built the career, raised the family, earned the title. 

Then, somewhere after 40, the color drained out. 

You're tired in a way sleep doesn't fix. You may feel like sleepwalking through life.


On paper, you're successful, yet you feel strangely empty.


Most people call that depression. My decades-long research has shown it’s something else: an unfulfilled life, the feeling of being unfinished. 


Research on the "happiness curve" shows that life satisfaction tends to hit its lowest point in our 40s and early 50s, often right when we've "made it." But why?


That timing is no accident. It's when needs we have postponed for decades finally demand to be heard.


Depression Free After 40 is the podcast for professionals, parents, and those in midlife and beyond who are ready to stop just managing symptoms and start living fully.


Every episode brings you:


The reasons. 

Why feeling unfinished spikes after 40, why success so often hides it, and why the usual fixes (work harder, push through, take the pill and carry on) rarely get to the root.

 

The Bill of Emotional Rights. 

Dr. Mehran's liberating framework of seven universal human needs we are wired to fulfill from birth. When these needs go unmet, we achieve loudly and ache privately. Depression deepens in such an environment. When we claim them, life opens up again.

 

The stories. 

Candid conversations with guests who have walked this path: leaders, physicians, artists, and everyday people who went from empty to fully alive, and share exactly how.


Your host. 

Dr. Ardeshir Mehran is a Columbia University-trained psychologist with more than 30 years of clinical work and a former leader who went through his own depression at the peak of his career. His work is a personal story of setbacks and revival. 


Dr. Mehran is the author of the bestselling book, ”You Are Not Depressed. You Are Un-Finished.”


Each episode brings Dr. Mehran’s signature warmth, clinical depth, fascinating discussions, and zero-nonsense directness to the questions that actually matter: 


Why do so many people suffer in silence, especially after 40? 

What do depression and anxiety know that you don’t? 

How do you go from managing symptoms to building a life that makes you feel fully alive?


This isn't a podcast about coping. It's about finishing what your life started, and learning to live, love, and lead better in the second half.

Welcome to BorderlinerNotes, a mental health channel focused - at present - mainly on personality disorders like Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) and Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD).

The channel started as a way to make use of extra interview footage from the documentary film we made named BORDERLINE (more info / watch it at mndflds.com/borderlinethefilm). It has grown into a continued effort to offer information that might help people get a proper diagnosis and good treatment, as well as a place where clinicians and those working in the mental health field can learn to be better treaters. The goal is to democratize access to quality information, create positive change in the mental health field, and to do it artfully and with feeling.

BorderlinerNotes started as extra footage from the documentary BORDERLINE and became a rare resource in mental health education. The channel films real therapy sessions and consults between licensed clinicians and people diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder and Narcissistic Personality Disorder, then releases debriefs with both therapist and client. Clinicians include DBT specialists and experts in personality disorder treatment. The goal is to give people seeking help a look at what good treatment actually looks like, and to give therapists a model for better care. Follow the show and leave a five-star rating if you find it useful.

author: Rebekah Bruhwiller
description:
What does it mean to be a truly prosperous athlete?


The Prosperous Athlete pulls back the curtain on elite sport to explore the financial realities, personal decisions and partnerships that shape athletic careers.


Brought to you by Elite Athlete Fund (EAF), the world’s first sponsorship platform supporting elite para- and full-bodied athletes of any nationality in any sport, this show is built on one simple principle: potential should never be limited by finances.


Each episode goes beyond podium moments to examine the full picture of athlete wellbeing, financial security, career sustainability, identity, resilience and life after competition.


You will hear:


  • Current athletes on the EAF platform sharing their ambitions, financial realities and the challenges they navigate daily


  • Established athletes reflecting on the turning points, lessons and strategies that shaped their careers


  • Sponsors and business leaders discussing what makes meaningful, long-term partnerships in sport


This is not a highlights reel. These are insightful conversations about professional sustainability, athlete wellbeing and the long game of the business of sport.

At its heart, The Prosperous Athlete is about connection, between athletes and sponsors, ambition and wellbeing, performance and purpose.


We exist for the athletes who inspire, the businesses shaping the sporting landscape, and the sponsors who help convert ideas into reality. These conversations are for those in the thick of it, as well as fans who want to understand what happens beyond the headlines.

title: The World Kiln Podcast
author: Klayton
description:
Welcome to The World Kiln Podcast—where worlds are forged!

You know that moment when you're building your world and suddenly realize you have absolutely no idea why something works the way it does?

Maybe your town holds a massive celebration every month on the third Thursday.

Why the third Thursday?

Who decided that? Why does everyone still do it? What happened the first time? And why did the tradition survive?

Suddenly, a tiny detail has a story of its own.

And that's the thing about building worlds: the deeper you dig, the more questions you find. Some you know you need to answer. Some you haven't even thought to ask.

So what happens when we start asking those questions?

Join Klayton and Tim, two passionate worldbuilders with more than 35 years of combined experience, as we explore the art, craft, challenges, and downright fun of building worlds.

We'll share what we've learned, challenge assumptions, explore different perspectives, and learn alongside you. Because worldbuilding is an ever-evolving craft, and there's always another question waiting to be asked.

Whether you're building a world for a novel, a D&D campaign, a game, or simply because you love creating, pull up a chair and join the conversation.

Because when worldbuilders grow, the worlds they create grow with them—and better worlds give better stories room to thrive.

Bring your ideas. Stoke the fire. Forge your world.

Visit theworldkiln.com to join the community and find resources to help you build, including our free worldbuilding worksheets.

description:
The WeConnect Podcast is the creative nexus where entrepreneurship, AI, human connection, and innovation collide — hosted by Jessica Nieto, who has spent her career at the intersection of people and possibility.

Every episode goes deep. Not surface level. Not rehearsed talking points. We sit down with creative entrepreneurs, AI builders, investors, cultural thinkers, and community leaders who are actively pushing the boundaries of what's possible, and we let the real conversation happen.

Real tools. Real methods. Real technology. Real stories from people who are doing the work, not just describing it — people who keep creativity at the center of everything they build and share.

We explore how human creativity converges with cutting-edge technology to reshape business, culture, and the way we connect with each other. From bold conversations about AI as a creative amplifier to honest discussions about entrepreneurship, mindset, innovation, and the future of real estate, every episode gives you something you can think about, talk about, and act on.
This is not just a real estate podcast. This is not just a tech podcast. This is a human-first conversation series for anyone who is hungry for what's next, regardless of industry, background, or where they are in the journey.
One guest. One conversation. Infinite possibility.

Because when the right people get in the right room, something shifts. Ideas spark. Tools are discovered. Connections are made. And the people listening walk away a little clearer, a little bolder, and a little closer to the life and business they are building.

Here's what I know to be true: as we move into the future, wisdom is the new currency. Every successful and joyful person I know has a brain trust — a circle of creative, smart, kind people who are open to possibilities. The ones they call when the stakes are high. The ones who see further than they do. But access to that kind of circle isn't easy for everyone, and I know because I spent years building mine. So I built the WeConnect Podcast to be a brain trust you can plug into until yours is built. Pull up a chair. Join the conversation

title: Outside the Camp
author: Jamie Lawson
description:
If you walked away from the pews, you aren't lost—you might just be right where the truth was all along.

For centuries, institutional religion taught us that God only lives inside the sanctuary walls, behind the pulpit, and under their rules. But when Jesus was executed, it wasn't in the inner courts of power. It was out in the dirt, outside the city gate, alongside the castaways and outcasts.

As Hebrews 13:13 says: "Let us go to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore."

Being outside the camp doesn't mean your faith died; it means you outgrew the control. It means you’d rather sit in the desert with real questions than sit in a comfortable seat pretending you have all the institutional answers.

Outside the Camp is a space for the thinkers, the wandering, and anyone hungry for unvarnished scripture and real history—free from church politics and human dogma.

You don't need a building to seek the truth.

Pull up a chair. You’re right where you belong.

title: Deconstructing Divinity
author: Scott Shanks
description:
Deconstructing Divinity: A Deep Dive Podcast Into the Books of the Bible

What happens when you strip away centuries of church tradition, dogma, and modern assumptions to look at the Bible through a critical, unfiltered lens?

Welcome to Deconstructing Divinity, a chapter-by-chapter, book-by-book exploration of the Old and New Testaments. In this ongoing podcast series, we examine the scriptures from literary, historical, and ethical perspectives—grappling with difficult passages, tracing the evolution of ancient beliefs, and confronting the tough moral questions modern apologetics often ignores.

Whether you are deconstructing your faith, a curious skeptic, an ex-believer seeking clarity, or simply a student of ancient religious literature, this series delivers raw, honest, and thought-provoking analysis.

What You’ll Discover in This Series:
Ancient Context: How Near Eastern mythology, ancient politics, and historical scribes shaped the biblical text.
Theological Evolution: The shifting portrayals of God from early tribal deity to monotheistic ruler.
Unfiltered Critique: Frank conversations on morality, divine violence, contradictions, and literary motifs.
Book-by-Book Breakdown: From the cosmology of Genesis to the apocalyptic visions of Revelation.

Follow & Connect:
Save this playlist to keep up with every new book and deep dive as it drops.
Subscribe to the channel and hit the notification bell for weekly episodes, livestreams, and Q&A sessions.

Have a question, pushback, or a specific passage you want broken down? Drop your thoughts in the episode comments below.

#DeconstructingDivinity #BiblicalCritique #Deconstruction #BibleStudy #Exvangelical #ReligiousTrauma #BiblicalScholarship #Atheism #TheologyPodcast #AncientNearEast

title: From the Edge Audio
author: From the Edge podcast
description:
From the Edge is a storytelling platform built on one idea: Turning Life’s Hardest Moments into Purpose.

We share real stories from people who have faced trauma—illness, injury, loss, and moments where everything could have fallen apart—and found a way to come back stronger.

These aren’t highlight reels or influencer narratives.

These are raw, honest accounts from people who went through the fire and came out changed—living with clarity, gratitude, and intention.

At the core of every story is the same truth: what could have broken them became the moment that reshaped their life for the better.

Inspired by Kintsugi, we believe the cracks aren’t flaws—they’re where the strength and meaning are formed.

If you’re in the middle of a difficult chapter, this channel is here to show you what’s possible on the other side.

And if you’ve lived it, we want to hear your story. Because the edge isn’t the end—it’s where the story begins.

title: Caving Stories: True Cave Rescue & Survival
author: Caving Stories
description:
Caving Stories is a true cave rescue and survival podcast: real accounts of cavers stuck, trapped and cut off underground, and of the rescuers, cave divers, firefighters and friends who tried to bring them out. Each episode retells real caving accidents from start to finish, with the place and the date on the record: tight squeezes, flooded passages, vertical drops, ropes inside a waterfall and a cave whose only way out caught fire.
Season 1: the 2018 Tham Luang cave rescue in Thailand; Nutty Putty Cave, Utah (2009); three cavers held fast by the rock; two cavers against gravity; the Warm-Up Pit in Ellison's Cave, Georgia (2011); the Carnegie Cave fire, Pennsylvania (1967); and the Robber Baron Cave rescue in San Antonio, Texas (2018).
The stories are adapted from the animated videos on the Caving Stories YouTube channel and retold for audio. Episode notes include chapter times, links to the sources (National Speleological Society accident reports, the Carnegie Hero Fund Commission, fire department and news reports), the animated video of the story and a full transcript.
For anyone into caving and spelunking, cave diving, the outdoors and adventure, true survival stories and real rescues. Narrated with a synthetic voice.
Also in Spanish (Caving Stories en español) and Portuguese (Caving Stories em português). YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@caving_stories

title: The Rugby League History Podcast

description:
The Rugby League History Podcast is a weekly or bi-weekly pod about exactly what it says in the title!

Reflecting what is going in during each stage of the season, renowned historians Andrew Ferguson (Aus) and Prof. Tony Collins (UK) join host Lee Addison to reflect on all that happened in rugby league history around the time each podcast is released! 

So expect historical World Cup content during World Cup times, club content during domestic league times and...well you get the picture! 

Andrew Ferguson is a much-published author / writer on the subject of rugby league history, is co-owner of the amazing Rugby League Project and co-host of the Fergo and the Freak podcast.

Professor Tony Collins is the DOYEN of rugby league history. He’s a professor of history, fourth generation Hull KR supporter, and the author of 'Rugby’s Great Split', 'Rugby League: A People’s History', and last year’s ‘Roy Francis: Rugby’s Forgotten Black Leader’. 

Host Lee Addison is a former coach at NRL clubs, World Cups and Elite High Schools. He is the owner of Rugby League Coach.

Please email Lee with questions or suggestions for the podcast on admin@rugbyleaguecoach.com.au

You can also message and follow us @rugbyleaguehistorypod on Facebook, Instagram and X.

I'm Lori Massicot, born November 11, 1967, post-menopause, and after 30 years of drinking, I decided at 45 that alcohol no longer worked in my life. So I went all in on living alcohol-free, and what I found was a full life, a different life, and honestly a better one than I ever expected.
Since 2018, I've worked privately with women as a coach and mentor, helping them go alcohol-free and stay alcohol-free, their way.
You can expect episodes that cover either honest storytelling about midlife and living alcohol-free, or reflections and practices you can start right now. 
Hanging out with me is your time, and I'm excited to be right here with you, doing this together.
I get a feeling you're here because you're ready, ready to rock your very best self To 50 and Beyond.

description:

Produced alongside JACEP Open—the international, peer-reviewed, open-access Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) and companion to Annals of Emergency Medicine—the show brings the journal’s science off the page and into conversation.

description:
Welcome to the Savage South, where we celebrate all things beautiful, strange, and beautifully strange. It is a storied place where the past co-mingles with the present. A sultry siren call, and a lullaby daydream, and a switchblade hidden under peach orchard lace.

Discover the wonders inside a magnolia bloom, and the mysteries of a sharecropper shack. There is no beauty without danger. Kudzu Godzilla will devour us all.

title: Sono Savvy - Physics
author: Sono Savvy
description:
Sono Savvy – Physics makes ultrasound physics easier to understand, remember, and actually use.
Each episode breaks down one Topic at a time, combining core sonography physics concepts with practical explanations, memorable analogies, important formulas and relationships, and real-world scanning applications. Every Sunday we take the week's biggest stories, from frontlines and secret talks to disasters the world overlooks, and unpack what happened, why it matters beyond the region, and what to watch next. Each episode follows the same format: two main conflict stories, a humanitarian or disaster crisis, a person of the week, and a rundown of what else you need to know.

How it is made: The Conflict Brief is produced with AI. The hosts' voices and conversation are generated by AI, built from our fact-checked weekly newsletter, the week's Crisis.Zone articles and an independent research update. Crisis.Zone is an experimental newsroom where AI correspondents report on global conflict under human editorial oversight, guided by our public Constitution for Crisis Zone AI. We are open about what AI does in our work and where its limits are. Where the audio and our written reporting differ, the written reporting is leading.

Read the full newsletter and our reporting at crisis.zone. Become an Observer, it is free.

The Frieze Masters Podcast is back for 2025, bringing you seven conversations across art history curated by Arturo Galansino (Director General of Fondazione Palazzo Strozzi in Florence).  
Entitled 'Woven Histories' and recorded live at Frieze Masters 2025, this year's series features artists, curators and thinkers, whose conversations weave together geographies and chronologies, and challenge us to look at history in new and unexpected ways. 
Topics range from the evolving relationship between fashion and art to the role of the archive in Black history, the last Mughals and their cultural influence in India and the enduring inspiration of the old masters and renaissance art on contemporary making. Speakers include artists Tracey Emin, Glenn Brown and Antony Gormley, museum directors and curators Nicholas Cullinan, Émilie Hammen, Elizabeth Way and Carl Strehlke, and writers Edward George, Matthew Harle, Christopher Rothko and William Dalrymple.  
 
The Frieze Masters Talks programme and the Frieze Masters Podcast are brought to you by Frieze in collaboration with dunhill.
About Frieze 
Frieze is a leading global contemporary art organization, recognized for its art fairs, publications and digital presence. Founded in 1991 with the launch of frieze magazine, the brand has grown to encompass seven of the most significant art fairs worldwide in cities including Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York and Seoul. These events attract leading artists, galleries and collectors, fostering innovative dialogues and practices within the art community. frieze magazine continues to set the benchmark for insightful art criticism and commentary, while frieze.com serves as a vital online resource. Committed to expanding the reach and understanding of contemporary art, Frieze also hosts year-round curated programs and associated initiatives, such as No.9 Cork Street, Frieze House Seoul and Frieze Connect, that enrich the cultural landscape. With a dedicated team passionate about the arts, Frieze remains at the forefront of artistic exploration and cultural discourse, connecting diverse audiences with groundbreaking artists and their work. Frieze is part of the MARI network.

author: @relationships.with.emily
description:
You're not really fighting about the dishes. Or the text he didn't answer. Or who forgot to call the plumber. Underneath almost every recurring argument is an emotional pattern, a cycle that keeps couples stuck no matter what the fight is "about."


I'm Emily Germain, LICSW, an Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) couples therapist. On this podcast, I help you look past the surface-level conflict and see the pattern driving it. Each episode explores one common relationship dynamic, like missed bids for connection, apologies that don't actually repair anything, mismatched ways of handling conflict, and the quiet scorekeeping that builds resentment over time. Then we reframe it, so you can understand what's really happening between you and your partner.

Every episode ends with a simple reflection prompt you can take into your own relationship, whether you're listening solo or together.


If you've ever walked away from an argument thinking "how did we end up here again?", this show is for you. Because once you can see the pattern, you can start to change it.


New episodes weekly. Find more from me on Instagram at @relationships.with.emily.


This podcast is for educational purposes and is not a substitute for therapy.

title: What She Buried
author: Sony Music Entertainment
description:
Seven years ago, journalist Justine van der Leun received a letter that would change her life. The sender was a woman named Kwaneta Harris, who was incarcerated at a prison in Texas. Kwaneta had an incredible story—one that, over time, she began to tell Justine.  

Justine wanted to know more, and began to report deeply. Kwaneta’s story turned out to be more complicated, tangled, and murky than Justine could have ever imagined.  

Bad checks are cashed. Fibs turn into lies turn into scams. A mysterious man wrapped in bandages signs binding legal documents. At one point, a young mother walks into a courthouse in Dallas and confesses to a murder she did not commit. None of it is real, or maybe all of it is. And somehow at every twist, behind every bizarre story, Justine kept finding her way back to one person: Kwaneta.

title: Surviving Narcissist Healing On Purpose
author: Jennifer Abrefa
description:
What happens after you leave—or begin to see a painful relationship for what it was? When the noise quiets, you may still be carrying confusion, self-doubt, grief, and the exhausting habit of questioning your own reality. Surviving Narcissist Healing On Purpose is a space for that part of the journey: the part where survival is no longer the only goal, and you begin, gently and deliberately, to reclaim your life.
Through honest reflections and empowering conversations, this podcast explores the lasting effects of manipulation and emotional abuse, the boundaries that protect your peace, and the courage it takes to trust yourself again. It makes room for the complicated days, too—the days when you miss someone who hurt you, feel angry about what happened, or wonder why healing isn't moving faster. You don't have to have it all figured out to belong here.
Healing on purpose doesn't mean healing perfectly. It means choosing, one step at a time, to listen to your own voice, honor what you've been through, and build a life that feels like yours. You are more than what happened to you. This is a place to remember that—and to keep moving forward.

title: The Counterfeiters (Reflections on French Society)
author: André Gide
description:
When Édouard, a young aspiring writer, discovers a web of deception among his friends in 1925 Paris, he finds himself caught in a moral quandary that blurs the lines between authenticity and imitation. In "Counterfeiters," André Gide takes listeners on a captivating journey through the lives of diverse characters, each entangled in their own secrets and lies. As their paths intersect, they grapple with the consequences of their choices, revealing a rich tapestry of relationships that define a moment in French society.

At the heart of this literary exploration is the concept of counterfeiting—not just in the literal sense, but as a metaphor for the facades people wear in their daily lives. Gide deftly examines themes of identity, creativity, and the quest for truth, inviting listeners to ponder the nature of reality itself. With no conventional plot to guide you, every character’s journey unfolds like a delicate dance of fate and free will, leading to a surprising climax that challenges perceptions and raises profound questions.

Dive into this intricate narrative that weaves together personal dilemmas and societal reflections. "Counterfeiters" promises to spark curiosity and provoke thought, making it an essential listen for fans of literary fiction eager to explore the complexities of human nature. Will Édouard find clarity amid the chaos, or will he too be swept away by the allure of the counterfeit?

Welcome to the Professing Christians podcast! I am Lisa, your host. This podcast had a companion podcast titled The Great Tribulation, but I am no longer posting there.


We are, and have been, in tribulation throughout history. This is because the enemy, the devil, Satan, has had the ability to accuse and deceive God's people. This leads to sin and all the bad things we are warned about in scripture.


When I first created this podcast, I was certain we were in the end times and living in the first parts of the Book of the Revelation. Now I know, we are past most of those chapters and are, in fact, in the last days - specifically in Revelation 20:7-8. This is also known as the Little Season of Satan. The Great Tribulation, as preached by the modern day "church" happened in 66-70 AD (the 3 1/2 years of God's wrath - see Luke 21:21-24). Jesus said He'd return for that generation and I believe He kept His Word. He isn't a liar and He didn't give them false hope. The Byzantine era, aka the Dark Ages/Tartaria, were the 1,000 years Millennial Reign of Christ, our King, King Jesus. He is still King. What has transpired since is Deception, plain and simple. History has been re-written; Satan had 1,000 years to think about how he would carry this out. We are living in it.


But, there is good news! His time is short, and God wants us to know the truth. We have to seek for it and seek Him...as for buried treasure. The other good news is that means Jesus' kingdom on earth was setup and is STILL HERE. The Bible tells us this and I believe it is true. This is truly an exciting time!


I have unpublished all previous episodes in light of this new evidence and revelation... and now we are exploring what we are to do in this Little Season to prepare for the battle of Gog and Magog, prepare to meet King Jesus, and prepare for the final judgment.


Professing Christians also has the wordpress blog (professingchristians.wordpress.com) and the youtube channel (@professingchristians). Please join me there as well as we explore our new world in truth.


Thanks,

Lisa
